title: MIMIC-IV-ED v2.2 (PhysioNet)
findings: vitalsign table holds irregularly timed vital signs with charttime; free-text vitals removed during de-identification; credentialed access; also on BigQuery.
limitations: Project page not opened; counts come from the server audit of 2026-11-03.

title: Multimodal Clinical Monitoring in the Emergency Department (MC-MED) v1.0.1 (PhysioNet)
findings: Quotes the data paper: 'only publicly available ED dataset is MIMIC-IV-ED'.
118,385 adult visits, monitored beds of the Stanford adult ED, Sep 2020 - Sep 2022; numerics as 1-minute means.
v1.0.1 release note: a small number of de-identified MRNs were re-generated.
Credentialed access; PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0.

title: PhysioNet content listing, topic=emergency
findings: Lists MIMIC-IV-Ext-MDS-ED 1.0.0 (credentialed), MC-MED 1.0.1, ER-REASON 1.1.0 (contributor review), MIMICEL 2.1.0, MIETIC 1.0.0 (9,629 triage cases), Gout ED chief complaint corpora, etc.

title: MIMIC-IV-Ext-MDS-ED / MDS-ED: Multimodal Decision Support in the Emergency Department (arXiv 2407.17856)
findings: Built from MIMIC-IV-ED tables and MIMIC-IV-ECG; inputs within 90 min of ED arrival (demographics, biometrics, vitals, labs, 12-lead ECG); targets 1,428 ICD-10-CM codes and 15 deterioration measures; v2 reports 71,098 patients, 121,195 visits, 129,095 samples.
limitations: Project page and paper not opened.

title: yaleemmlc/admissionprediction (GitHub README)
findings: Results/5v_cleandf.RData: 560,486 x 972 de-identified dataframe, each row a visit.
Triage vitals averaged; historical vitals/labs summarized as last/min/max/median; no license stated, only a citation requirement.

title: Predicting hospital admission at emergency department triage using machine learning (PLoS ONE 13(7): e0201016)
findings: Three EDs in one health system; adult visits March 2014 - July 2017; triage and patient-history features; outcome hospital admission.

title: NHAMCS emergency department documentation (NBER data items; NCHS doc16_ed, doc17_ed)
findings: Visit-level records with initial vital signs and triage level; from 2016 asks whether vitals were taken after triage.

title: Benchmarking emergency department prediction models with machine learning and public electronic health records (Sci Data 9:658)
